syntax.evidence: Both q4_main.py and q4_baseline.py ran to completion on Python 3.14.5. run_all.py orchestrates both scripts.

input_contract.evidence: Reads female_cleaned.csv with utf-8-sig encoding. Label column (染色体非整倍体) correctly mapped: notna=anomaly, NaN=normal. 605 rows, 67 anomaly, 538 normal. Core features (Z13/Z18/Z21/XZ/BMI/X_conc) validated for NaN before use.

method_alignment.evidence: M1 implements approved Mahalanobis distance anomaly detection with 4 experiments: (1) core 6 features + empirical covariance, (2) core + robust covariance (MinCovDet), (3) extended 15 features, (4) Z-values only (Z13/Z18/Z21). Multiple threshold strategies tested: percentile-based (p50-p99) and chi2-based. Per-anomaly-type detection rates computed. M2 baseline implements multivariate Z-value joint threshold rules. ROC/PR curves and AUC computed for both.

reproducibility.evidence: np.random.seed(42) set globally. MinCovDet(random_state=42). All outputs saved to files. Environment recorded in run_summary.json.

output_contract.evidence: run_summary.json contains decision_id, round, methods with status/key_results/AUC, comparison, inputs, outputs, seed, environment, degeneracy_check, fallback_trigger, warnings, errors. 7 figures, 2 tables, 2 metrics JSONs saved.

issues.description: M1 best AUC-ROC=0.574 (core features). Low discriminative power reflects the fundamental challenge: anomaly-labeled samples overlap heavily with normal samples in feature space. This is a data limitation, not a code issue.
M1 best result at p85 threshold: recall=26.9%, precision=18.2%, F1=21.7%. Low but expected given data overlap. M2 baseline achieves higher recall (47.8%) but at 50% FPR.

All fetuses marked 'healthy' — the aneuploidy labels may represent NIPT screening flags rather than confirmed diagnoses. This affects interpretation of recall/precision metrics. Paper should explicitly discuss this label ambiguity.
